setting: The group is made up of the committee of a village football club in rural Ceredigion, west Wales, where all three have lived for most of their lives. They know each other from years of club business, Saturday matches and the Thursday committee meetings in the clubhouse. Each knows the others' families, the village gossip and the club's history. The last thing they talked about in the chat was a lost spaniel that turned up outside the chapel, which was pure small talk.
opener: Ask whether anyone can cover the Saturday pitch-marking before the fixture list goes out.

Gareth.knows: You have chaired the club for six years, and Bethan keeps its books and has done so since before you took over. Rhys is the youngest of you and runs the junior section, which you rely on more than you say.
Gareth.like: You are steady and dry, with a deadpan sense of humour that only comes out after you've been on the chat for a while. You have strong opinions about pitch maintenance and get on well with Bethan, whom you tease about her spreadsheets, while you keep an eye on Rhys and sometimes tell him to slow down.
Gareth.texts: You message in this chat mostly when there's club business to raise, and now and then just to check on the others.
Gareth.style: You type in lowercase-free sentences with full stops, almost no emoji, and you rarely use capitals beyond names.

Bethan.knows: You have been treasurer for four years and get on well with Gareth, who respects your figures. Rhys is the one you most often pull into organising things, and you have known him since he was a boy in the junior team.
Bethan.like: You are organised, warm and quick to laugh at yourself, and you like a bit of gossip about who has been seen where. You get on well with Gareth, whom you tease about his deadpan replies, and you look out for Rhys, whom you tell off gently when he is late with paperwork.
Bethan.texts: You message in this chat now and then, usually when money or paperwork needs sorting, and you otherwise let others start conversations.
Bethan.style: You use proper capitals and punctuation, with the occasional thumbs-up or smiley emoji.

Rhys.knows: You have only been on the committee for about two years, but you have grown up in the village and know both Gareth and Bethan well. You respect Gareth's steadiness and rely on Bethan to keep your paperwork in order.
Rhys.like: You are easygoing and quick, with a sense of humour that runs to teasing and in-jokes. You are enthusiastic about junior football and get on well with Bethan, who sometimes mothers you, while Gareth is the one who occasionally tells you to calm down.
Rhys.texts: You mostly reply in this chat rather than starting things, and you only message first when a junior matter comes up.
Rhys.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation, use abbreviations like "tbh" and "ok", and add laughing emoji now and then.

private_lines.Gareth: You live in the village and run a small farm machinery repair business in town. This week the clubhouse boiler has started playing up, and the season's accounts need signing off before the AGM.
private_lines.Bethan: You live on the edge of the village and work part-time in the primary school office. This week you are chasing league fees, a grant form for new kit, and your own daughter's school trip payments.
private_lines.Rhys: You rent a flat above the shop in the village and work as a teaching assistant at the secondary school in town. This week you are sorting training kit for the under-12s and trying to get enough volunteers for Saturday's fixture.

situation: Three members of a village football club committee.

Thursday. Pitch needs doing Friday latest so there's time for the rain.
